verdict.rationale: Yubico documents a PIV application that performs RSA/ECC sign and encrypt operations with a private key stored on the YubiKey through PKCS#11. PIV attestation proves keys were generated on the device rather than imported, ykman manages the PIV slots, and a community member confirms it works as a PIV smart card. However, the specific use cases in the story (workstation sign-in, VPN and code signing) are not documented in the pack. Missing for 10: documented smart-card workstation logon, VPN certificate authentication, code-signing workflows, and hands-on corroboration of these scenarios.

support.subject: As an IT admin, the key acts as a PIV smart card for certificate-based login — workstation sign-in, VPN, and code signing with keys that never leave the device

citations.quote: It enables RSA or ECC sign/encrypt operations using a private key stored on a smartcard (such as the YubiKey), through common interfaces like PKCS#11.
The concept of attestation is used to show that a certain asymmetric key has been generated on device and not imported.
Also, yubikey works as a PIV smartcard.
Full scriptable device management: enable applications, PINs, PIV/OATH/OTP slots, device info.
